name: as_strided
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied VERBATIM from the supplied schema: aten::as_strided(Tensor(a) self, SymInt[] size, SymInt[] stride, SymInt? storage_offset=None) -> Tensor(a). This representative signature is NOT exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for the operator, including every registered overload (all supplied registered schema strings are listed verbatim here: aten::as_strided(Tensor(a) self, SymInt[] size, SymInt[] stride, SymInt? storage_offset=None) -> Tensor(a)), keyword arguments, return identity/aliasing, error behavior, mutation and gradient behavior; tests must never be removed or narrowed to this one signature. Semantics from the tests: as_strided is a zero-copy metadata/view rewrite that returns a new tensor object viewing self's existing storage with the requested size, stride and storage_offset, reading or moving no element data (values are therefore compared exactly, zero tolerance). An explicit storage_offset is absolute inside the underlying storage, while omitting it or passing None inherits the input tensor's own storage_offset (e.g. 17 for a windowed input). The result aliases the input storage, so writes through the result are visible through the input at the same positions; the input's own metadata is left untouched and the result is a distinct object (not the input itself, not an in-place rewrite). Lazy conjugate/negative bits are preserved, and gradients scatter (summing where the view overlaps itself) back into the input's storage. Invalid layouts (rank mismatch between size and stride, negative size, negative stride, negative storage_offset, index range beyond the storage) raise RuntimeError. as_strided never broadcasts its operand, so stride-0/expanded layouts are covered as input views rather than via broadcasting. Non-JSON ATen defaults: storage_offset uses JSON null to denote the optional SymInt? default None. Representative parameter kinds/defaults are supplied metadata and must not be guessed or inferred from a single benchmark call.
